a1_answer:
STANDARD PRACTICE: Prevents extruder surge by installing a mechanical metering hopper with vibratory de-aerating/compacting plates to homogenize feed bulk density before the barrel inlet.
MECHANISM DEPARTURE: Replaces the mechanical density-compaction element with a feedback-driven variable-height gate (shim stack) that adjusts the free-flow cross-sectional area of the feed chute in real-time to maintain a constant mass flow rate regardless of upstream bulk density fluctuations.
FAILURE-PHYSICS CONNECTION: Surging is driven by fluctuations in the mass flow rate ($\dot{m}$) caused by $\rho_b$ variations; maintaining $\dot{m}$ constant via $A$ modulation decouples the extruder screw dynamics from the feed stock property variance.

PHYSICS CHECK: Mass flow rate through a gravity feed chute is $\dot{m} = A \cdot \rho_b \cdot v_{fall}$. Assuming $v_{fall}$ is constant for the specific hopper geometry (Stokes' regime for granular solids), $\dot{m} \propto A \cdot \rho_b$. To keep $\dot{m}$ constant when $\rho_b$ varies, $A$ must vary inversely with $\rho_b$. A variable-height gate (modulating $A$) provides the necessary inverse proportionality without relying on a compaction mechanism to alter $\rho_b$ itself.

IMPLEMENTATION BILL:
- COMPONENT: Variable-height gate assembly at the extruder feed inlet.
- MATERIALS: Standard food-grade stainless steel gate plates; existing actuator hardware.
- INSTRUMENTS: Existing downstream pressure transducer (P1, P2) and screw rotation speed sensor (already recorded in SCADA).
- PROCEDURE: Install the gate assembly; configure the PLC logic to calculate the required gate opening $A_{set}$ from the ratio of measured pressure to a baseline reference pressure.
- INPUT STREAM 1: Downstream barrel pressure ($P$) — ALREADY-RECORDED (stated in problem as the primary monitoring signal for surge detection).
- INPUT STREAM 2: Screw rotational speed ($N$) — ALREADY-RECORDED (stated in problem as the second signal used in standard monitoring).
- REFERENCE/BASELINE: Baseline pressure $P_{ref}$ corresponding to nominal bulk density $\rho_{ref}$ — DERIVED from existing historical SCADA logs of stable operation (stated problem implies historical data exists for commissioning standard monitoring).
- THRESHOLD: $\Delta P = |P - P_{ref}| > P_{surge}$ (stated surge threshold) triggers gate adjustment; $A_{set} = A_{max} \cdot (P_{ref} / P)$ — CALCULATED from the mass-flow physics relation.

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY):
- INSTALLABILITY: Same as standard (mechanical hardware at the same location); slightly higher complexity due to actuator, but avoids the high-maintenance vibratory plate wear issues.
- OPERABILITY: Fully automated; no operator intervention for density variations; standard for PLC-controlled lines.
- MAINTENANCE: Lower than standard (no vibratory mechanisms, fewer moving parts subject to clogging/wear compared to high-speed vibrating plates).
- COST: Similar material cost (stainless steel); actuator cost is offset by reduced maintenance and downtime associated with clogged vibratory plates. SAME burden class, DIFFERENT mechanism (feedback geometric modulation vs. active mechanical compaction).

EXECUTABLE TEST:
- PROTOCOL: Introduce batches of feed stock with known varying bulk densities ($\rho_{low}, \rho_{high}$) into the hopper. Monitor the extruder pressure $P(t)$ and mass flow $\dot{m}(t)$ during steady-state operation.
- INSTRUMENTS: Existing pressure transducers, existing flow meters.
- PASS/FAIL THRESHOLD: The standard deviation of the extruder pressure signal $\sigma(P)$ over a 10-minute window must remain below the stated surge threshold $P_{surge}$.
- DURATION: 30 minutes of continuous operation with alternating density batches.
- KILL CRITERION: If $\sigma(P)$ exceeds $P_{surge}$ or if the gate actuator reaches its mechanical limits while $\Delta P$ persists, the mechanism fails to decouple density from flow.
- VALIDATION: Verified against the physical relation $\dot{m} \propto A \cdot \rho_b$ using the already-recorded pressure baseline $P_{ref}$ to confirm that the gate area modulation inversely tracks the pressure deviation, thereby stabilizing $\dot{m}$.

CONSTRAINT BIND: The monitored indicator is the primary stated indicator: extruder pressure (surge detection). The screw speed is a secondary indicator used to normalize the pressure reading for process load, supplementing the primary signal. The solution does not introduce new sensors; it uses existing pressure and speed signals to drive a mechanical change.
